title: TXT parser drops numbered chapter titles when a repeated special subtitle follows
symptom: In the external novel corpus at `/Users/longshengxi/Downloads/小说测试集`, 《星际第一种瓜王！》 has real adjacent double-title sequences such as `第141章 番外一` followed by `番外一`, and `第142章 番外二` followed by `番外二`. Before the fix, parsed chapter titles contained `番外一` and `番外二` instead of the source boundary titles `第141章 番外一` and `第142章 番外二`.
root_cause: ChapterCandidateScanner correctly emitted both the numbered chapter candidate and the repeated special-marker candidate, and ChapterCandidateFilter kept both. ChapterCandidateMerger only merged adjacent `CHAPTER + CHAPTER` candidates, so it left the `CHAPTER + SPECIAL` pair separate. ChapterAssembler then skipped the first candidate because its body range was blank before the repeated short title, making the visible TOC use the second physical title line.
fix: Extend ChapterCandidateMerger to merge adjacent `CHAPTER + SPECIAL` candidates only when there is no meaningful text between them and the special title exactly equals the normalized tail after the numbered chapter prefix.
Keep the first physical title line as `ParsedChapter.title`, preserving the parser plan's double-title semantics.
Keep independent special chapters separate when body text appears before the special marker.
Add merger, parser, ImportCoordinator, and external-corpus regression coverage for numbered chapter titles followed by repeated special subtitles.
failed_attempts: Do not fix this in ChapterDetectionRules; detection already produces both candidates and changing special-marker detection would hide legitimate standalone `番外` chapters.
Do not implement the match as broad `contains`, `endsWith`, or prefix matching; the repeated special title must exactly equal the normalized chapter-title tail after the chapter suffix.
Do not merge `SPECIAL + CHAPTER` or pairs with meaningful body text between them; that would collapse independent `番外` chapters into neighboring numbered chapters.
impact: TOC titles and persisted imported chapters now keep the source's stable numbered chapter boundary while still dropping the repeated short subtitle line from chapter body text.
